title: Headline, About and top 3 roles, from proven answers only
purpose: Rewrite the profile in recruiter search words, claiming only what the proof answers support.
why: The profile is a claim. It should say only what the proof questions showed, in the words recruiters type when they search.

modules.title: Help the right people see your work

tasks.title: Headline: your role | the work you want next | three or four skills you can prove
tasks.done_when: Uses the version your answers support.

tasks.title: Put your links at the top of your About: GitHub now, your own site later
how: The first lines of your About are links, one per line, so a reader can see your work before reading anything else.
If you don't have your own domain for a portfolio site yet, leave that box empty. We set the site up later and add the link then.
tasks.done_when: Your GitHub link is the first line of your About on LinkedIn.

fields.label: Your portfolio site (only once it's live)

tasks.title: Write your About from the template, one part at a time
how: Fill in each box below in your own words, then paste them into your LinkedIn About in this order, under your links, with a blank line between parts.
The text in each empty box is a made-up example to show the shape. Replace it with your own story, and only claim what you can explain in an interview.
tasks.done_when: Every part is filled in and pasted into your LinkedIn About under your links.

fields.label: 1. One line on the problem you solve and what it gets the reader
fields.placeholder: I help small teams add AI to the systems they already run, without breaking what works.

fields.label: 2. Who you are: your role, your years, what you're strongest at, and the kind of problem you like most
fields.placeholder: I'm a software engineer with 4 years across TypeScript, Python and cloud. My sweet spot is being dropped into a codebase I didn't write, making it work, then adding the feature people actually asked for.

fields.label: 3. What you're building right now, and who it's for
fields.placeholder: Right now I'm building ClaimDesk, an assistant that drafts insurance claim decisions and waits for a person to approve anything that moves money. Every step is logged so a reviewer can check it.

fields.label: 4. Your background: the stacks you've worked in and one concrete thing you shipped, with a result if you have one
fields.placeholder: Before this I kept client apps running through contract placements, set up CI and test automation for a five-person team, and taught web development to beginners for eight months.

fields.label: 5. What you care about in how you work: three short bullets
fields.placeholder:
- Changes you can trace and undo
- Plain explanations for the people who use the system
- AI that asks a person before it does anything risky

fields.label: 6. The roles and work you want next: three short bullets
fields.placeholder:
- Forward deployed or integration work with customers
- Owning a feature from the problem to production
- Teams putting AI agents into real workflows

fields.label: 7. Who should message you, and about what
fields.placeholder: If your team has a system that works but nobody wants to touch, or you're bringing AI into one, I'm always open to talk.

fields.label: 8. What you offer: three or four bullets, each an area and the specifics
fields.placeholder:
- AI integrations: tool calls, approvals, audit trails
- Legacy cleanup: tests, refactors, safer deploys
- Full-stack delivery: TypeScript, Node, Python, REST APIs

fields.label: 9. Tools and tech, on one line, only ones you can talk about
fields.placeholder: TypeScript, Node.js, Python, Docker, PostgreSQL, GitHub Actions, AWS

tasks.title: Top 3 roles: 2–3 bullets each, problem → what you built or owned → result
Pin verified skills first; agent skills only if true
tasks.done_when: Top skills are the ones you can defend in an interview.
